title: A review of intelligent interactive learning methods
extended_summary:
This paper reviews recent literature on intelligent interactive learning (IIL) methods and technologies in e-learning, with a focus on how AI-enabled and adjacent technologies are being used to improve engagement, personalization, and learning outcomes. The authors frame IIL as an adaptive learning approach that uses intelligent components to respond to user input and improve performance over time.

The review is semi-systematic and covers literature published from 2018 to 2023, drawing on sources such as Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Hindawi, and Springer. Rather than studying one learner population directly, it synthesizes prior studies across higher education, MOOCs, language teaching, medical training, and other educational contexts, including applications of AI, cloud computing, IoT, big data/learning analytics, VR, AR, and gamification.

The paper concludes that these methods can improve interaction, motivation, personalization, and instructional efficiency, but each has practical limits such as insufficient evidence of impact, privacy concerns, limited engagement, lack of clinical trials for AR, and implementation or funding constraints. Overall, the authors argue that future intelligent learning systems should integrate interactive content and student-oriented support to address gaps in educational resources and assessment services.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a semi-systematic literature review using qualitative synthesis of prior studies, not a primary causal study or meta-analysis. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically described, but it does not meet stronger credibility criteria for causal inference.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests broad positive impacts of intelligent interactive learning, but it does not report pooled effect sizes or a single tested intervention. Reported impacts are therefore plausible but unclear in magnitude at the general-population level.

interventions.use_case: Semi-systematic review of intelligent interactive learning methods in e-learning, including AI-enabled systems, MOOCs, VR/AR, gamification, cloud computing, big data/learning analytics, chatbots, recommenders, and mobile learning applications.

finding.finding_summary: The review synthesizes prior studies suggesting that intelligent interactive learning tools generally improve user engagement, motivation, and social dynamics in e-learning. However, this is a narrative synthesis rather than a pooled estimate, so no overall effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Reported engagement, motivation, and social interaction outcomes across reviewed studies

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that AI-enabled and cloud-based learning systems can automate curriculum delivery, assessment, recommendation, and monitoring, improving teaching efficiency and reducing infrastructure burden. Examples include personalized learning platforms, automated learner support, and systems that help teachers monitor students during lessons and tests, but the review does not provide pooled effect sizes.
finding.measure: Reported instructional efficiency, automation of assessment/support, and teacher monitoring capacity across reviewed studies

finding.finding_summary: The review notes that ChatGPT and other AI language tools may improve students' reading and writing abilities, and that AI-supported language teaching can provide personalized feedback and content. These claims are based on the cited literature summarized in the review; no meta-analytic effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Reading and writing outcomes reported in prior studies on ChatGPT and AI language teaching
